sentences: Two M.2 drives can look identical, yet one can be ten times faster.
That's because M.2 is a shape, not a speed.
It's a small stick that screws flat onto your motherboard.
Some use SATA, the same link as a 2.5-inch SSD.
They top out around 550 megabytes per second.
Others use NVMe over PCIe lanes.
Even older ones reach about 3,500 megabytes per second, and newer drives pass 7,000.
To tell them apart, check the notches.
SATA sticks usually have two, B and M.
NVMe sticks usually have one, the M key.
The label tells you for sure.
And check your motherboard manual, because some slots only take NVMe.
More PC hardware explained on the channel.
